text:
alex: Heads-up from an onboarding run — C# sample shows bursty 429s when customers use very short STS TTLs and enable prefetch.

alex: Repro in staging: launch 10 tasks each iterating the Paginator with Prefetch=4, set STS TTL to 10s. After a minute we get repeated spikes of 429s.

nina: Can you paste the sample usage?

alex: Sure:
```csharp
var p = new Paginator("/v1/embeds", pageSize: 64, prefetch: 4);
await foreach(var page in p)
{
  _ = Task.Run(()=> client.EmbedAsync(page));
}
```

alex: The C# SDK's auth handler checks `if(token.IsExpired)` and kicks off refresh per request, no async dedupe.

kevin: Our JS had a promise-dedupe, Go used singleflight, Python patch incoming. C# parity missed it.

nina: Immediate mitigations: lower prefetch to 0 or set `MaxConcurrency=1` in sample app. Also add a lock around the refresh path in the sample.

kevin: Long-term plan: add a refresh Task dedupe to the C# auth middleware (store a Task in-flight, await it if present). Also add pause-on-auth-failure in the Paginator (small backoff and stop prefetch for N seconds after consecutive 401s).

alex: QA note: our CI has no token-rotation smoke for C# yet. Can we add a small test that simulates rotating creds and asserts only one refresh call per rotation window?

qa-bot: Test request logged: create `AuthRotation_SingleRefresh` in csharp-sdk CI — will spawn 8 workers and fake TTL=8s.

nina: Also will update onboarding docs: call out STS TTL tuning + sampleapp default prefetch guidance. Short-lived tokens (<30s) need client-side dedupe or lower prefetch.

kevin: PRs after lunch: github.com/redwood/csharp-sdk/pull/129 (auth-dedupe) and github.com/redwood/sampleapp/pull/92 (csharp prefetch note).

alex: Thanks team. Once PR merges let's run a couple staging ramps and watch gateway 429 metrics.
